title: I Want the Spirit of Power Within
description: I Want the Spirit of Power Within in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 223, “Spiritual Needs”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: I Want the spirit of power with-in, Of love, and of a health-ful mind: Of power to con-quer ev-ery sin; Of love to God and all man-kind; Of health that pain and death de-fies, Most vig-orous when the bo-dy dies.

lines: I Want the spirit of power within,
Of love, and of a healthful mind:
Of power to conquer every sin;
Of love to God and all mankind;
Of health that pain and death defies,
Most vigorous when the body dies.
O, that the Comforter would come,
Nor visit as a transient guest,
But fix in me his constant home,
And keep possession of my breast;
And make my soul his loved abode,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
